newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan top trade body lauds economic package.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan top trade body lauds economic package.

text.p: Pakistan's apex trade body on Friday welcomed a government economic reforms package that reduced several taxes and duties and said some incentives would boost exports.

"It is production- and export-oriented," Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FPCCI) president Ilyas Ahmed Bilour said hours after Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz unveilied the package in the National Assembly (lower house).
The package lowered the rates of income and corporate taxes, general sales tax, customs duties and announced measures to increase industrial production.
The lower taxes and duties would certainly reduce the cost of production and make products competitive abroad and thus increase exports, Bilour said in a statement.
"The reduction in customs duty ranging from 10 to 25 percent on goods prone to smuggling will bring more items under the legal import regime, curb smuggling and increase government revenue," he said.
The lower rates of income tax and corporate tax would increase profitability of companies, reduce tendency of tax evasion and increase government revenues, he said.
It was a big challenge to businessmen and industralists not only to increase production and exports but also to avoid any temptation to indulge in tax evasion or other malpractices, Bilour said.
However, he said the government should take concrete measures to tax agricultural income.

"The failure of the government to tax a sizeable section of the well-to-do population ( of agriculturists) will not enable it in reducing budget deficit, which continues to be a serious problem," Bilour said.
